step1_analysis.description: This circuit appears to be a sub-block of an adaptive bias network for an RF amplifier. It utilizes source followers (XM5, XM6) and current mirrors (XM3-XM4) to detect the envelope signal and adjust the bias accordingly to improve intermodulation distortion.

paper_reference.title: Analysis of Envelope Signal Injection for Improvement of RF Amplifier Intermodulation Distortion

dc_power.description: Total DC power consumption of the sub-circuit

sky130_expected.calculation: VDD * I_total. With 10k bias resistors and 1.8V supply, the current per branch is roughly (1.8V - Vth) / 10k ≈ 138uA. For 6 branches, total current is ~0.8mA. Power = 1.8V * 0.8mA = 1.44mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 2W reported in the paper is for the main power amplifier. This envelope tracking bias sub-circuit operates at baseband/envelope frequencies and consumes a small fraction of the total power.

voltage_gain.description: Voltage gain of the source follower path (N2 to N7)

sky130_expected.calculation: Source follower gain is gm * Rs / (1 + gm * Rs). It is slightly less than 1 (0 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The source follower configuration (XM5) inherently yields a voltage gain close to unity. The 16.5 dB reported in the paper refers to the main RF amplifier's forward gain.

envelope_bandwidth.description: Bandwidth of the envelope detector path

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the RC time constant of the source follower output resistance (1/gm) and the load capacitance.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The envelope bandwidth must be wide enough to pass the WCDMA modulation envelope (5 MHz to 10 MHz as reported in the paper) without significant attenuation or phase shift.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC gain, and transient response of the adaptive bias sub-circuit. Dummy load resistors are added to prevent floating nodes and establish DC bias currents.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Envelope Detector / Bias Circuit Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVIN N2 0 DC 0.9 AC 1 SIN(0.9 0.1 1MEG 0 0)
VBIAS N12 0 DC 0.9

* DUT
XM1 N1 N1 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N3 N12 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N5 N5 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 OUT N5 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 VDD N2 N7 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 VDD N3 N8 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}

* Loads to prevent floating nodes and set bias currents
R1 N1 0 10k
R3 N3 0 10k
R5 N5 0 10k
R7 N7 0 10k
R8 N8 0 10k
ROUT OUT 0 10k

.control
* DC Operating Point
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power

* AC Analysis
ac dec 10 1k 1G
let gain_db = vdb(N7)
meas ac gain_100k find gain_db at=100k
meas ac gain_10M find gain_db at=10Meg

* Transient Analysis
tran 10n 5u
meas tran v_max max v(N7)
meas tran v_min min v(N7)

quit
.endc
.end
